To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
high school GPA, performance self-efficacies, and grade goal were the best correlates of university GPA.

(a) the strongest correlates of academic performance were measures of cognitive capacity (high school GPA, ACT and SAT), self-efficacy for performance, and grade goal; (b) personality traits, motivational factors, self-regulatory learning strategy use, students' approaches to studying, and psychosocial factors were all significantly related to academic performance but to a lesser extent; (c) the magnitude of the correlations between these constructs and academic performance was medium-sized or larger for self-efficacy and

1) the average, weighted correlations for the non-intellectively related variables were small to medium in size; 2) the strongest non-intellectually based correlate was academic self-efficay, which had a medium-sized correlation with GPA; and 3) the strongest intellectively based correlate was high school GPA, which had a large correlation with GPA.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the psychological correlates of university students’ academic performance.
the question of whether and to what extent non-intellectively based measures are associated with university students' academic achievement.
the psychological factors that predict academic performance.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
, although the predictive validity of cognitive ability and prior academic performance are well established, non-intellectively based predictors of academic performance are also promising.
the strongest predictor of GPA is the GPA from the last year of high school.

, while intelligence, academic ability, and academic performance have been found to be strongly correlated, it is the non-intellectively based factors that are the best predictors of academic performance.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the strongest predictors of academic achievement are those that are most closely related to academic achievement.
the strongest correlates of university students academic performance were their prior academic performance and self-efficacy.
students' non-intellectively based factors are more predictive of GPA than are traditional measures of intellective ability.
The main takeaway from our work is that

, in the absence of a comprehensive, empirically validated model, researchers and educators must continue to rely on a combination of traditional measures of prior academic performance, cognitive ability, and non-intellectively based predictors of academic success.
, while students' cognitive abilities and prior achievement are strong predictors of academic performance, non-intellectively-based constructs also play a role.
the most robust correlates of university students GPA are those that are directly tied to the academic domain.
